knowledge:
- key_parameters: Y=Matrix of gene expression data (features as rows, samples as columns) ;; X=Model matrix of the design ;; coef.h=Integer index of the coefficient(s) associated with the null hypothesis (H0) ;; batch=Factor specifying the batch structure of the samples ;; initialised.obj=An initialized random rotation object returned by initBatchRandrot or initRandrot ;; R=Number of random rotations to perform ;; statistic=A user-defined function that takes the data matrix and other parameters, performs the analysis pipeline (e.g., batch correction and model fitting), and returns a vector of test statistics ;; cormat=List of correlation matrices for sample replicates within batches, used for linear mixed models
- alternatives: Standard parametric p-value estimation (e.g., using limma directly on batch-corrected data), which is discouraged because batch correction methods introduce dependencies among samples, leading to non-uniform (skewed) null distributions of p-values.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you need to perform differential expression or other linear model-based analyses on high-dimensional normally distributed data (such as microarray or RNA-seq data) after applying a separate batch effect correction method (e.g., ComBat or removeBatchEffect), or when dealing with repeated measures/mixed models with batch structures.
- pitfalls: Using scale-dependent statistics (like raw parameter estimates/coefficients) instead of scale-independent statistics (pivotal quantities like t-values) in the statistic function ;; Failing to take the absolute value of the t-statistic in the statistic function, which is required for pFdr to correctly calculate two-tailed p-values ;; Assuming independent samples across batches when there are correlations (requires specifying cormat in initBatchRandrot or using initRandrot) ;; Using too few rotations (R) when features are highly dependent, although pooling statistics in pFdr helps reduce the required R.

workflows.name: linear_model_batch_correction
workflows.intent: Perform batch effect correction and linear model analysis while obtaining unskewed, rotation-based p-values and false discovery rates (FDR).
input: edata (matrix of gene expression data with features as rows and samples as columns)
pdata (dataframe of phenotype and batch information for each sample)
workflows.stages:
1. Create the design model matrix using model.matrix.
2. Initialize the batch random rotation object using initBatchRandrot, specifying the null hypothesis coefficient and batch covariate.
3. Define a custom statistic function that performs batch correction (e.g., ComBat) and extracts absolute t-statistics from a linear model fit (e.g., limma).
4. Run the rotation and calculate statistics using rotateStat.
5. Calculate resampling-based p-values and FDRs using pFdr.
workflows.code:
mod1 <- model.matrix(~1+phenotype, pdata)
rr <- initBatchRandrot(Y = edata, X = mod1, coef.h = 2, batch = pdata$batch)
statistic <- function(Y, batch, mod){
  Y <- sva::ComBat(dat = Y, batch = batch, mod = mod)
  fit1 <- limma::lmFit(Y, design = mod)
  fit1 <- limma::eBayes(fit1)
  abs(fit1$t[,2])
}
rs1 <- rotateStat(initialised.obj = rr, R = 10, statistic = statistic,
                   batch = pdata$batch, mod = mod1)
p.vals <- pFdr(rs1)
fdr.q  <- pFdr(rs1, "fdr.q")
fdr.qu <- pFdr(rs1, "fdr.qu")
fdr.BH <- pFdr(rs1, "BH")

workflows.name: contrast_analysis_batch_correction
workflows.intent: Test specific contrasts in batch-corrected data using random rotations to obtain unskewed p-values.
input: edata (matrix of gene expression data with features as rows and samples as columns)
pdata (dataframe of phenotype and batch information for each sample)
workflows.stages:
1. Create the model matrix and define the contrast matrix using limma::makeContrasts.
2. Transform the model matrix to include the contrast as the last coefficient using contrastModel.
3. Initialize the batch random rotation object using initBatchRandrot.
4. Define a custom statistic function that performs batch correction, fits the contrast, and extracts absolute t-statistics.
5. Run the rotation using rotateStat and calculate p-values using pFdr.
workflows.code:
mod.groups <- model.matrix(~ group)
contrasts1 <- limma::makeContrasts("2vs3" = group2 - group3,
                                   levels = mod.groups)
mod.cont <- contrastModel(X = mod.groups, C = contrasts1)
init1 <- initBatchRandrot(edata, mod.cont, batch = pdata$batch)
statistic <- function(Y, batch, mod, cont){
  Y.tmp <- sva::ComBat(dat = Y, batch = batch, mod = mod)
  fit1 <- limma::lmFit(Y.tmp, mod)
  fit1 <- limma::contrasts.fit(fit1, cont)
  fit1 <- limma::eBayes(fit1)
  abs(fit1$t[,1])
}
res1 <- rotateStat(initialised.obj = init1, R = 20, statistic = statistic,
                   batch = pdata$batch, mod = mod.groups, cont = contrasts1)
p.rot <- pFdr(res1)

workflows.name: mixed_model_batch_correction
workflows.intent: Perform random rotation for datasets with repeated measures (random effects) and batch structure using linear mixed models.
input: edata (matrix of gene expression data with features as rows and samples as columns)
pdata (dataframe containing batch, tissue, and individual/replicate identifiers)
workflows.stages:
1. Estimate the correlation matrix (cormat) between sample replicates within batches.
2. Create the design model matrix.
3. Initialize the batch random rotation object with the estimated cormat using initBatchRandrot.
4. Define a custom statistic function that removes batch effects (e.g., removeBatchEffect) and fits linear mixed models (e.g., lme) to extract absolute t-statistics.
5. Run the rotation using rotateStat with parallel processing and calculate p-values using pFdr.
workflows.code:
covs1 <- function(., df1, i){
  df1$d1 <- .
  me1 <- lme(d1 ~ tissue, data = df1[i,], random = ~1|individual)
  getVarCov(me1, type = "marginal")[[1]]
}
covs1 <- sapply(spl1,
                function(samps)rowMeans(apply(edata, 1, covs1, df1, samps)))
cov1 <- matrix(rowMeans(covs1), 2, 2)
cormat <- cov2cor(cov1)
cormat <-  diag(5) %x% cormat
cormat <- list(cormat, cormat, cormat)
mod1 <- model.matrix(~1+tissue, pdata)
rr1 <- initBatchRandrot(Y = edata, X = mod1, coef.h = 2, batch = pdata$batch,
                        cormat = cormat)
statistic <- function(Y, batch, mod, df1){
  Y <- limma::removeBatchEffect(Y, batch = batch, design = mod)
  apply(Y, 1, function(j){
    df1$d1 <- j
    me0 <- nlme::lme(d1 ~ 1, data = df1, random = ~1|individual, method = "ML")
    me1 <- nlme::lme(d1 ~ tissue, data = df1, random = ~1|individual, method = "ML")
    abs(coef(me1)[1,2] / (sqrt(vcov(me1)[2,2])))
  })
}
rs1 <- rotateStat(initialised.obj = rr1, R = 4, statistic = statistic, 
                  batch = pdata$batch, mod = mod1, df1 = df1, parallel = TRUE)
p1 <- pFdr(rs1)
